item.title: Shared Memory Consistency From Scratch Part 1: Causality
item.description: Hardware and programming language memory models are rightly seen as difficult subjects, yet the confusion that surrounds them is a side effect of poor understanding, even amongst experts, and not part of the intrinsic difficulty. While I can't invent the universe to explain shared memory consistency from scratch, I can design a novel computer architecture, together with a set of atomic instruction, to highlight the core problems and how to overcome them. The architecture will be weaker than anything that exists today, and serve as a proving ground for various abstract memory models, including the now ubiquitous C++ memory model. Along the way, I'll introduce new semantics to facilitate efficient synchronization and reasoning about correctness, as well as discuss how to fix problems with the C++ model. more

item.title: Daniel Skogly's blog | Motivating Myself for Exercise by Arbitrarily Withholding Things I Desire
item.description: I love the Souls-games by From Software, not only for the satisfying gameplay, but also for the incredible worldbuilding that I’ve never experienced the likes of in any other game series. There are some things in Demon’s Souls (the first Souls-game I played) game design that simply amazed me - I didn’t know NPCs were allowed to do act like that it games! Also, there’s something to be said for game developers willing to put big portions of a game on the other side of hidden walls that a player might miss entirely, and quest lines / endings requiring the player to really explore the world and consequences of their actions without much or any handholding. So why haven’t I played further than Bloodborne (2015)?
